Apparently, according to the NS Barristers Society (NSBS), under civil law it is within acceptable ethics to not disclose information critical to valuation of a property, if not in a court of law. one_star_reviews.text:
Building our home with Paradigm Custom Homes was an extremely stressful and disappointing experience. If I could do it over again, I would choose a different builder. Based on our experience, I cannot recommend Paradigm Custom Homes.
My biggest concern throughout our build was the lack of clarity and transparency around pricing, allowances, upgrades and what was actually included in the price of our home. We were new to the custom-home building process and relied on the builder to clearly explain these things. Unfortunately, we often felt we were learning important details only after decisions had been made or additional costs were already arising.

Our windows are one example. Early in the build, we chose black window frames. Jeff later acknowledged by email that he had originally quoted double-pane windows and advised us of the additional cost to upgrade to triple-pane. We agreed by email to the additional cost for the black frames and triple-pane windows. At that point, we didn’t understand the importance of formal change orders and assumed this agreed-upon upgrade would be incorporated into the overall price of our home. It wasn’t until much later, just before signing our contract, that we received the change order and learned that the window upgrade—thousands of dollars—had not been incorporated into the price we had been working with.

There were other situations that added to our frustration. Our engineered drawings showed acrylic stucco and decorative stone, but we later learned these were considered upgrades at an additional cost. Our HVAC system was listed in our specifications as included, yet we later learned that costs associated with installing and connecting the system were being charged against our electrical allowance. Our specifications also called for a LiftMaster garage door opener, but a Chamberlain was installed instead without a change order approving the substitution.

There were also times when I felt pressured to make expensive decisions very quickly, including being told that our windows needed to be ordered that day. Building a home involves too much money to feel rushed into major decisions.

My advice to anyone considering a custom build is to educate yourself before you begin and document absolutely everything. Do not assume that something shown on your plans or listed in your specifications means what you think it means. Ask exactly what is included, what is considered an upgrade, what each allowance is expected to cover, and insist on receiving change orders as changes happen—not months later. Keep your own running total and confirm in writing that every change has been added to or deducted from the total price. Also confirm your window specifications immediately, including whether they are double- or triple-pane.

Building our home should have been one of the most exciting experiences of our lives. Instead, I found the process stressful from beginning to end, and by the end of our build I had lost trust in the process. I deeply regret choosing Paradigm Custom Homes. If I could make the decision again, I would choose a builder where I felt there was clear communication, transparency and trust throughout the entire process.

Based on our experience, I would not build with Paradigm Custom Homes again, and I cannot recommend them.

This was, without question, one of the worst professional service experiences I have ever had.

I provided my tax documents to H&R Block well before the filing deadline and trusted them to handle my return professionally. My file was being handled by Ms. Subothini Janahan. For approximately 10 days, I repeatedly tried to contact her and received no proper response.

Then, on the final day to submit my tax return, I was finally contacted and essentially told: “Sorry, I couldn’t do your tax return because I don’t know how to do it.”

Absolutely unbelievable.

If you did not know how to complete my return, why was I not told this when I first submitted my documents? Why hold my file for days, ignore my attempts to reach you, and wait until the filing deadline to tell me you were unable to do the work?

When I asked why I had not been informed earlier, the only meaningful response I received was basically “sorry.” No solution. No accountability. No reasonable explanation.

Because of their handling of my file, my tax filing was delayed. This was not a minor inconvenience — this involved an important government filing with an actual deadline.

What made the experience even worse was the complete lack of accountability from management. I specifically requested that a manager contact me so someone could explain how this was allowed to happen. The manager never even called me.

That tells me everything I need to know about how seriously this location takes customer service and responsibility.

Mistakes can happen. What I cannot accept is taking someone’s documents, failing to communicate for days, waiting until the deadline to admit you cannot complete the work, and then having management completely ignore a request for an explanation.

I would strongly recommend staying away from this location. After this experience, H&R Block would be an absolute last resort for me. Even in an emergency, I would think twice before trusting them with something as important as a tax return again.

If I could leave 0 stars, I would do it without hesitation.

Completely unacceptable service, terrible communication, and absolutely no accountability.

one_star_reviews.text:
We are extremely disappointed with how our experience at this TD branch has changed since the new management took over.

Our brokerage has banked with this branch for years, and during that time we built a great relationship with Malik, the previous branch manager. Malik took the time to understand our business, knew our history with the bank and treated us like a valued business client. There was a level of trust and mutual respect that was built over many years, and that was a big reason we continued banking with TD.

Since Malik left, it feels like all of that history and goodwill has disappeared. The relationship we spent years building seems to mean very little under the new management.

We understand that banks have policies and procedures, but there should also be some value placed on a client’s history, track record and the relationship they have built with the bank. Things that were previously handled with reasonable discretion based on our history are now treated completely differently.

That’s what has been most frustrating. You spend years being loyal to a bank and building a relationship, only to realize that the relationship can essentially start from zero when the manager changes.

Malik was an excellent example of what relationship banking should look like, and unfortunately our experience since his departure has been the complete opposite.

We have decided to leave TD and move our brokerage’s banking to another institution that we hope will place more value on long term business relationships.

It’s disappointing after all these years, but we no longer feel there is a reason for us to remain loyal to this branch when that loyalty is no longer being reciprocated.

SAVE YOUR MONEY. READ THIS BEFORE BOOKING.

I called this salon BEFORE going in specifically to confirm the price of an acrylic full set. I was told $55, which included one colour. I explained that I wanted a white-and-gold design and was told the additional charge for the gold would be $15, bringing the total to $70.

I CONFIRMED THIS PRICE BEFORE I EVEN WALKED THROUGH THE DOOR.

Then somehow, at the end of the appointment, the price magically became $90.

So what exactly was the point of calling ahead and confirming the price?

And the pricing issue wasn’t even the worst part.

The manicure preparation was extremely poor. My girlfriend’s nails were not properly cleaned or prepared. Her nails weren’t properly cut, the hangnails weren’t taken care of, the cuticles weren’t properly pushed back or trimmed, and the filing/shaping was rushed.

The entire service was finished in roughly ONE HOUR.

Her hands were also handled roughly. A manicure is supposed to involve care and attention, not someone treating your hands like they’re an inconvenience standing between them and the next customer.

And here’s the part that really bothered me:

There was another woman who had already been there WELL before us getting her pedicure done. By the time we were finished, she was only THEN getting her manicure started.

Meanwhile, our entire service had apparently been rushed through in an hour.

That tells me everything I need to know about the priorities here.

I’ll give credit where it’s due: the nails themselves came out nice. The white and gold design looked good.

But pretty nails don’t magically erase sloppy preparation, rough handling, rushed service, and a price that changed after I had already confirmed it beforehand.

I actually spoke to the staff about the price because I wasn’t going to stand there and pretend I hadn’t specifically called ahead and confirmed the amount.

If you’re going to charge $90, say $90 BEFORE the customer sits down.

If you’re going to charge $70, charge $70.

Don’t give one price over the phone and somehow produce a completely different number when it’s time to pay.

And if you’re going to work on someone’s hands, actually take care of their hands.

The finished product may photograph well, but the experience behind it was honestly unacceptable.

NICE NAILS. TERRIBLE SERVICE. QUESTIONABLE PRICING.

I wouldn’t return, and based on this experience, I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone who actually cares about proper nail preparation, gentle service, and transparent pricing.

one_star_reviews.text: Most respectful man I have ever met.

UPDATE – September 11, 2026:
Gateway responded publicly to this review asking me to contact them by email so they could “take a closer look” and assist me. I emailed the address they provided on August 25 and included the information regarding Kafee’s aftercare. More than two weeks later, I have received no response whatsoever.

Unfortunately, this makes their public response feel more like an attempt to appear responsive on Google than a genuine effort to address what happened. I gave them the opportunity to follow up privately, as they requested, and they simply did not respond.

I am therefore leaving my original review and rating unchanged.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
We had a very upsetting experience with Gateway Pet Memorial during an extremely difficult time.

On June 27, we had to say goodbye to our beloved Kafee at the emergency vet. Gateway sent us an email that evening asking us to confirm her aftercare wishes by June 29. I saw the email the next day, but while grieving, I didn't read carefully enough to realize there was such a short deadline.

For something so time-sensitive and irreversible, I don't believe an email alone is sufficient. Emails can be missed or go to junk mail, and grieving families may simply not be in the state of mind to deal with these decisions immediately. If there is no response, there should be a phone call before proceeding.

What hurts us most is that we wanted to keep Kafee's paw print, just as we have paw prints from our other pets who have passed. By the time we realized what had happened, it was too late. Kafee is now the only one whose paw print we don't have.

An urn can be replaced; a paw print cannot. My husband and I are heartbroken that we lost this opportunity forever because there was no personal follow-up.

I sincerely hope Gateway changes this procedure so another grieving family doesn't experience the same regret.

We came for an appointment with our one-month-old baby. We were seen quite quickly, and we appreciate that. However, what happened afterward was an extremely traumatic experience for us as parents.

During the procedure to remove mucus from our baby’s nose, the nurse was very rough and aggressive. Our baby has never cried like that before. The suction was inserted deeply and abruptly, causing our baby extreme distress. After the procedure, half of our baby’s face became covered with red spots, and our baby was extremely upset.

We felt that our baby was not treated with the necessary gentleness and care that should be provided to a newborn. The way the procedure was performed was unacceptable to us.

When we showed the doctor the severe redness around our baby’s eye, the doctor tried to open the eye by applying force, even while our baby was sleeping. We were shocked by this approach.
After this visit, our baby could not be comforted for a long time, and we, as parents, experienced significant emotional distress. We came here seeking help, but unfortunately, we left feeling traumatized rather than supported.

We will be filing a formal complaint regarding this experience because we believe the way our baby was handled requires further review. Healthcare professionals working with newborns must provide careful, gentle, and compassionate care.

Based on our experience, we cannot recommend this facility to other parents of young babies.

I was very disappointed by my experience with Foster's Moving and Storage. I had done a lot of research and they were highly recommended off of Reddit but my experience did not align with all the positive reviews.

I was quoted $800 for a 4 hour move for a 600 sqft apartment to a 419 sqft apartment with a $95 dollar charge for a parking permit. The move was 2 blocks away from the original apartment.

They took 6.5 hours and charged me $1515 (which is an absurd price for the size of move and nearly double the quoted amount).
I specifically picked Foster's because the quote was a reasonable price and was much better than their competitors.

The movers were going at an extremely slow pace and blamed for my packing even though they had multiple styles of dollies for moving and they also blamed the distance to the elevator, even though the distance was not far to the elevator and they tried to ask for 3 key fobs for building access, even though they already had 2 key fobs which is the standard amount of fobs given for a unit.

I was frustrated because I spent a long time labelling all of my boxes carefully and they were just plopping boxes down randomly in whatever spot in my new smaller apartment with no care for the labels that I had carefully crafted to let the movers know where to put the boxes.

When I called to let the company know that I was upset, I was brushed off and wasn't allowed to finish my complaint and just told to send an email to an address, which I found to be very demeaning.

My experience left me very frustrated and it made the whole move day a very stressful day overall. I will not be using Foster's Moving and Storage again and will be advising others not to use their services as well.

one_star_reviews.text:
Last month I had to say goodbye to my cat Nina, and the prices here honestly still shock me when I think back on it.
I took her to my regular vet first. $130 just for the emergency fee, plus treatment, so $500 total. She gave it her best guess but it didn't work. So I ended up here.
Right away it was $268 for the emergency consult and $80 for bloodwork, and that's before they'd even treated anything. They also told me if she needed to be hospitalized it'd be $1700 a day, and an x-ray would run almost $800 on top of that. The vet said her chances of survival were minimal anyway — but honestly, I would've tried harder to find out for sure if the fees weren't so high. By the time everything was said and done — consult, bloodwork, meds, euthanasia — the bill here was $928.99. Add what I already paid my regular vet and I was out around $1500, and I still lost her.
I want to be fair, the staff were genuinely kind. This isn't on them. It's the pricing structure that's the problem. You're basically forced to choose between going into serious debt or letting your pet go, and that's a horrible position to put people in when their animal is suffering.
If you're thinking of bringing your pet here, ask for a full quote before agreeing to anything. Prices add up fast.
RIP Nina 🩶

Subject: Complaint regarding appointment cancellations and poor service (Date: October 4, 2026)
Dear Clinic Management,
I would like to bring to your attention the extremely disorganized conduct of your staff and the unacceptable treatment I experienced today.
At 9:40 AM, I booked a 30-minute consultation with a psychotherapist for 1:00 PM.
At 11:00 AM, I received a call and a message from Nursultan proposing that the appointment be moved to 12:00 PM. I agreed to this proposal.
Subsequently, I was informed that I needed to urgently fill out a complex form prior to the appointment—a requirement that had not been mentioned when I originally booked. Due to my severe mental state, I politely explained that I could not complete it on my phone right then, but promised to fill everything out on-site by arriving at the office a bit early.
In response, the doctor, Kiana Maida, stated that she does not accept new patients at all and refused to see me. I was referred to the clinic director, who could only schedule an appointment for a week later.
For someone seeking urgent psychotherapeutic help, such disorganization, the abrupt cancellation of an appointment, and the rescheduling to a week later cause immense stress. Instead of support, I was met with a judgment of my condition at your clinic.
I request that you investigate this situation, address the matter with your staff, and inform me regarding the handling of this complaint.
Sincerely,
Ivan Shumeyko

Our experience at The Public Pint House was appalling.  Our order was so badly mixed up multiple times and was never completely solved and our server was very incompetent.

What we ordered : ½ nachos, 2 piece fish and chips platter, fried chicken sandwich with Sriracha aoil on the side and poutine, and chicken fingers with fries.

What we got was ½ nachos and one piece of fish with poutine (on the same platter) and Sriracha aoli on the side.

When our server brought the food she asked if we needed anything else, so we said, yes, the chicken fingers with fries, the other piece of fish with the coleslaw and tartar sauce as advertised, and the fried chicken sandwich.  She removed the fish and poutine and after a rather long wait later we got a platter with a single piece if fish and fries.  The fish was dry and over cooked.

After another long wait we had to ask a different server about our meal.  Our server brought us a cup of ketchup and an apology, but not the rest of our order.

After another attempt to get the rest of the meal, our server finally brought the chicken strips and fries along with a grilled chicken burger with bacon and the poutine.  We pointed out the wrong burger and our server said she would go talk to the kitchen.  Half an hour later she stopped by our table to ask how everything was and if we needed anything, to which we said we were still waiting for the chicken sandwich.  She said she would check on it and brought it right over, it was cold and the poutine was soggy, so it had clearly been sat at the pass for a while.

They initially overcharged us for our meal but then comped the fish and chips explaining that even though the menu says two pieces with coleslaw and tartar sauce it is in fact only one piece of fish that is slightly larger.  They need to update their print menu rather than deceiving customers and provide much better customer service.

Our server was Martina and honestly, if this was not her first shift, it should be her last.

one_star_reviews.text:
Updated Review – August 2026

Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend Serenity Massage Therapy Clinic. I attended approximately 17 appointments here and never expected my experience to end this way.

The issue began after I accidentally missed my June 19, 2026 appointment. I fully acknowledge that keeping track of the appointment was my responsibility. The disagreement arose afterward when I was told the clinic had called me at approximately 10:05 a.m. and left a voicemail.

I checked my phone and found no missed call or voicemail from Serenity at that time. I later obtained records directly from my phone service provider, and the records available to me also do not show an incoming Serenity call around 10:05 a.m.

There was a reason I questioned this. Serenity’s own records document that on November 15, 2025, I was late for an appointment. On that occasion, the clinic called me, I saw the missed call and responded. Because I lived approximately two minutes away, I arrived within about five minutes and was still able to attend.

I recall using that experience as an example during our later discussion. However, Serenity’s interaction record states that I gave an example about being late for a dentist appointment. I dispute this. I was referring to my previous Serenity appointment, which is documented in their own records.

I also found the appointment reminder system inconsistent. Several historical reminders I retained for morning appointments were sent around 23 hours beforehand, even though the clinic requires at least 24 hours’ notice for cancellation. The messages were marked “NO REPLY – Reminder” and did not require confirmation. I still accept responsibility for missing my appointment, but I believe this is relevant context.

I politely asked on two occasions whether I could show my phone records—on June 19 and again when speaking with the clinic owner on June 22. When the clinic declined, I respected that decision and did not attend the clinic. I was therefore very disappointed to later see myself described in their interaction record as aggressive and “demanding” proof.

There was disagreement and some talking over one another, but I did not swear, threaten anyone or use derogatory language. The clinic later ended the therapeutic relationship and stated that it believed my communication had been “verbally abusive toward our staff.” I strongly dispute that characterization.

I later formally requested correction or clarification of disputed information and provided supporting phone records. Serenity declined to change its characterization but attached my correction request and supporting information to my file as a statement of dispute.

What disappoints me most is that I did not feel my concerns or evidence were meaningfully considered. I understand that a clinic has the right to end a therapeutic relationship, but I personally would not return to a clinic where I did not feel heard.

After approximately 17 completed appointments, I found the way this situation was handled extremely disappointing and, in my personal experience, unprofessional. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Serenity Massage Therapy Clinic.

This review reflects my personal experience, recollection and the records available to me.

We felt that our baby was not treated with the necessary gentleness and care that should be provided to a newborn. The way the procedure was performed was unacceptable to us.

When we showed the doctor the severe redness around our baby’s eye, the doctor tried to open the eye by applying force, even while our baby was sleeping. We were shocked by this approach.
After this visit, our baby could not be comforted for a long time, and we, as parents, experienced significant emotional distress. We came here seeking help, but unfortunately, we left feeling traumatized rather than supported.

We will be filing a formal complaint regarding this experience because we believe the way our baby was handled requires further review. Healthcare professionals working with newborns must provide careful, gentle, and compassionate care.

Based on our experience, we cannot recommend this facility to other parents of young babies.

Extremely disappointing experience with Coppin Forest Estates.

Before making the trip, I checked Google, which clearly showed the sales office as OPEN. I drove approximately 55 km specifically to visit the development, only to arrive and find the door locked and nobody there.

I called the main number and was told that there should be an agent at the sales office or a phone number posted on the door. There was a number on the door, but when I called it, the person who answered said they had no idea what I was talking about. There wasn’t even an agent’s name posted.

After waiting for approximately ONE HOUR, I finally received a call from an agent who informed me that visits are by appointment only. When I explained that Google clearly showed the sales office as open and that I had driven 55 km and waited an hour, rather than apologizing for the inconvenience, her response was simply that the website clearly states otherwise.

No apology. No acknowledgement of the wasted trip or the hour I spent waiting. Just an extremely rude and dismissive response.

If your Google listing tells potential customers that your sales office is open, you cannot expect people to somehow know that they need an appointment. At the very least, the information should be consistent and someone should take responsibility when it isn’t.

For a development selling multimillion-dollar luxury homes, I would expect a much higher level of professionalism and customer service. This experience was enough for me to lose interest completely. I would never bother going back.

When potential buyers are treated this way before they’ve even purchased a home, it certainly makes you wonder what the service would be like afterward.

one_star_reviews.text:
⚠️ Extremely disappointing experience

I came here because I genuinely wanted to adopt a dog and give an animal a good home. I first arrived around 9 AM because Google said the place was open, only to find out that 9 AM was apparently for the clinic and not adoptions. I was told to come back at 12, so I did exactly that.

When I came back, I called and was told that I would need to come another day and that they would call me to make an appointment. Then, while I was waiting and texting my mother, a staff member came outside and started questioning us about what we were doing there, where we lived, and other personal information. My brother was also questioned.

What made the experience especially upsetting was that I felt we were being treated with suspicion based on our appearance. We are Arab, and the way we were questioned made me feel like we were being treated as if we were there to steal a dog rather than people genuinely trying to adopt one. We were even told that our parents needed to be there because apparently they didn't believe we had a home.

On top of that, staff took pictures of our vehicle/license plate, which made the whole situation feel even more uncomfortable and suspicious.

If there are specific requirements for adoption, that's completely understandable. But those requirements should be communicated clearly and respectfully to everyone. People who come to adopt an animal are there because they care about animals and want to give one a home. Making people feel unwelcome, suspicious, or judged because of their appearance is unacceptable.

I left feeling extremely disappointed and uncomfortable. I hope management takes this seriously and looks into how potential adopters are being treated.

I would not return to this location.

I patiently waited in line when I first arrived, but I was not greeted. I was simply asked why I had come into the store. The employee assisting me appeared to be more focused on the fact that his shift was ending and quickly passed me off to another staff member.

The employee I was passed to was already assisting another customer, so I patiently waited again. She then walked to the back of the store without saying anything, leaving me standing there still waiting for assistance. When another employee finished helping a customer, he proceeded to assist someone who had arrived after me.

At that point, I mentioned that I had been the first person waiting and still had not received proper assistance. The employee explained that they were short staffed and went to the back to see what the other employee was doing. By this point, there were approximately five other customers waiting in the store, not including me.

Eventually, the employees came out along with the manager, Marty. What was particularly frustrating was that while the staff were clearly struggling to keep up with customers, the manager had apparently been sitting in the back the entire time.

When Marty finally came out, his demeanour was disrespectful and passive-aggressive. Rather than stepping in to support his staff or resolve the situation, he asked me what I needed and provided little to no assistance. I felt completely brushed off and unsupported.

I ultimately had to tell him that, as the manager, he should be helping his employees, especially when they are clearly struggling due to being short staffed, and taking responsibility for getting things organized and ensuring customers are properly assisted.

I ended up leaving and going to the Orléans location instead, where I was treated with respect and received extremely helpful service.

After this experience with Marty, I will not be returning to the St. Laurent location. I have also made a formal report to higher management within the company. Hopefully, this location receives the leadership and customer service support it clearly needs, because the experience I had was unacceptable.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing customer service and misleading information regarding box pick-up scheduling.

I called on August 7 and again on August 23 specifically to ask if there were specific pick-up dates and whether I needed to schedule ahead of time. I was repeatedly told “PICK UP EVERYDAY.” I also confirmed that someone needed to be available between 9 AM and 6 PM to sign the papers and hand over the box.

Because I was told pick-up was available every day, I planned to have my box picked up on Thursday, August 27. I called again today, August 26, to confirm.

I was then told, “Sa Saturday po pick-up.”

When I questioned this, the representative, (I will disclose his name once their company has reached out), kept saying:

“Pick-up everyday nga po, ma’am, kaso puno na po slots, so Saturday.”

Then he told me:

“Sana po nagpa-schedule kayo ahead of time.”

Excuse me? I DID call ahead multiple times. That was exactly why I called on August 7 and August 23 — to ask about the schedule and make sure I could plan accordingly.

If “PICK UP EVERYDAY” actually means “we pick up every day, BUT you still need to schedule ahead because the daily slots can be full,” then SAY THAT CLEARLY to customers.

Instead, I got the literal, "pilosopo" interpretation of “PICK UP EVERYDAY” — yes, technically you pick up every day, but apparently you still need to schedule ahead, which I was never properly told despite calling multiple times. Very ridiculous.

What made the experience even worse was the complete lack of empathy or accountability. There was not even an apology for the inconvenience. I had to point out to him myself how ridiculous the situation was before he even acknowledged the inconvenience.

I am now potentially losing an entire day of work because of information that your representatives gave me. I called ahead. I asked questions. I confirmed multiple times. I did my part.

The issue isn't that the schedule was full. I understand that availability can be limited. The issue is the poor communication, contradictory information, and lack of empathy when the mistake became clear.

Customers call ahead because they have work, responsibilities, and schedules to plan around. If customers need to reserve a specific slot weeks in advance, tell them that clearly. Don't repeatedly say “PICK UP EVERYDAY” and then blame the customer for not scheduling ahead when they have already called multiple times asking about it.

I would strongly suggest that you train your people properly, be transparent with customers, and provide accurate and complete information from the beginning. Good customer service also means having empathy and taking accountability when your own communication causes inconvenience to the customer. Reliable just became Unreliable because of this. Very frustrating.

Based on the website and our previous experiences with other camps, we understood that the available activities and facilities were included in the cost. We only learned after arriving that we were expected to organize and manage many of the activities ourselves, choose which activities to use, and request staff assistance to facilitate them. The beach rules, activity options, usage requirements, and any additional responsibilities or fees should have been clearly communicated before payment.

We also experienced some concerns with on-site staff professionalism. Staff appeared overwhelmed at times, and one staff member spoke to adults in a disrespectful and confrontational manner. The issue was the need for proper training, supervision, and professional communication with adult guests.

There were also safety and cleanliness concerns. Garbage remained in the campsite's trash bins overnight, and we saw a bear near the garbage area beside the restaurant. We were concerned that there did not appear to be bear-resistant garbage containers in place.
Finally, some cabins and beds had inappropriate sexual writing and drawings left by previous campers, including markings dating back several years ( ex2017), which suggests that more regular cleaning and maintenance are needed.
Overall, Camp Eden has a beautiful setting and several positive qualities, but respectful pre-arrival communication, better staff training, stronger waste and wildlife management, and improved maintenance would make a significant difference to the guest experience.

I am appalled by the behavior of the Patient Navigation Lead at BrainStim. A role centered on patient navigation requires a high degree of empathy, patience, and respect. Instead, I was met with shocking rudeness and hostility during a highly stressful medical journey.

Hostile Environment: Instead of feeling supported and guided, I felt judged and anxious every time I had to interact with him.
